notes.title: HAPPY NEW YEAR!
notes.content:
HI there!
Did i ever say that i'm forever grateful for all the support you guys gave me? No?
well,

[b]THANK YOU, FOR REAL. THANK YOU SO MUCH.[/b]

Sometimes life is hard, sometimes life is easy, but no matter what i'll continue to make games for you all. Maybe some of my future games will suck, but don't worry, i'll always try to improve and do better. I'm rly glad to have this small but amazing community of followers, this rly makes me want to continue to create new games, and its much more important than money to me.

So, whats in store for 2023? Well, the sequel to REDO!, of course!

Here is a not-so-precise roadmap for SESSIONS 2023.

Jan - dev
Feb - new trailer, dev
mar - dev
apr- Demo, dev
may - dev
Jun - Updated demo, new trailer, steam fest
jul - dev
aug - dev
set - Final trailer,dev

oct ~ dec = full release.


btw, happy new year!

notes.title: Untitled
notes.content:
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34329075/d0c1ef5413cf0539b417166b99ebab85856c321b.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34329075/5f64d5cfd9d20df9b6b1aabfc620a69a9618487e.png[/img][/url]


Hello guys, i just want to say sorry for the radio silent. I'm waiting for the right moment to show something big that i've been working for a while. I'm not ready to show it yet, that's why i've been silent. But i think i should at least talk about the enhanced edition.

REDO! the enhanced edition is not coming anymore. Why? I worked for more than one year redoing all the original game, in the end, I felt that I had changed lots of things  and that players would not like this new version because of it. on top of that, I would need to work even more fixing bugs, and listening to feedback... for a game that was already finished and ppl liked it(Original REDO!)... in the end, I just didn't have the motivation to keep working on the same game again plus I was deeply depressed because of things in my personal life.

So, all the work on the enhanced edition is going to waste? Hell no, in fact it is being used to build something even bigger.

Again, sorry for everything. I'm trying to do my best, but i'm just one person, but i promise i'll deliver something to compensate the enhanced edition.

Before the end of the year i'll come here to share this new big information. For now, just be a bit more patience, i'll do my best.

Just a small tease:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34329075/80bc172f024edf14cf70bec29c882e03315c15f4.png[/img]

notes.title: Question about input buffering
notes.content:
hey guys, what's up? i have a question for you!
i need to know what you think about the input buffering in REDO!
input buffering is  when you save a input to be used after another action take place.
ex: you roll and in the middle of the roll you press the attack button. When you finish rolling, the input(attack) will happen.

do you think:

a) It's ok the way it is right now

b) less input buffering

c) more input buffering

d)no input buffering at all(you can only do another action, after the actual action is over)

notes.title: Full release!
notes.content:
Hello, it's me again, the cutest dev you know.

REDO! is finally done(I think).

I think I fixed all the bugs, but I wouldn't be surprised if I forgot something. But don't worry, I'll continue to give support to the game.

there are some things that I would like to implement, like more save slots and gamepad remap, but unfortunately, some of those systems are very old when I began to make the code of the game, and changing it would break a lot of things. I know, it's my fault, but I learned a lot and will not do the same mistake again in future games.

I choose to not change some of the unpopular mechanics because I didn't want to deviate too much from my original intentions.

I'm kinda ok the how the game is, it could be better in some aspects of course, but I think it's ok for a first game done by one person.

I already started a new project, so keep an eye open for news.

Again, thank you for all the support.

notes.title: new update!
notes.content:
Hey! the new mode is finally here! There will be some bugs, but i'm working right now to get things fixed. To access the new mode, first you need to finish the normal campaing, then the "new game+" option will be available.

The main point of this mode it to offer a "second run" with a different level design and some few dialogues and enemies. It's nothing mind blowing, but if you liked the normal campaing, well now you have something "new" to play haha.

It's something i would like to see in more games, to be honest. With some changes in the level design and enemy position you can create a lot of interesting new situations.

I'm still balancing things, so you may find some sections almost impossible, but i'll keep working on it.

what next?

now, i'll keep polishing this mode and fix some old bugs that i ignored until now. you can expect daily updates.  Next thing will be the full release. After all the major bugs and balacing issues are solved i will probably create a new trailer and then release the game.

Well, thats it!

enjoy!


**** I had some problens with the italian translation in the hard mode, so it may take a few more days to the italian translation to be available. Sorry!
but english and portuguese is fine!

notes.content:
Hello!

The next update for REDO! will be the biggest and most important until now.

the hard mode won't be just a more challenging mode, it will expand the replayability of the game.

features of the hard mode:

- some new enemies

- Hard enemies will appear early in the game.

- changes to the level design( you'll need to do a new rote)

- aside  from key weapons and  key items, all weapons will have new locations and will be randomized (I'm not 100% sure this will work, need more testing)

-expanded ending

-new achievements


As the early access roadmap says, this mode will be released in April. I'm not sure if I'll be able to release in the beginning of April, so I think middle of April is more accurate.

if everything goes according to the plan, REDO! should leave Early access still in April!

Thanks for the patience!

notes.title: Redo! sneaks into the dusty tunnels of early access
notes.content:
Ever since playing an early prototype, I’ve been looking forward to today’s launch of Redo!. It’s an aggressively bleak metroidvania about a lone woman attempting to survive and maybe even find another human after an apocalyptic robot rebellion. Combat is panicky, weapons feel insufficient, and the machines themselves are strange, twisted and exceptionally deadly. The early access launch is effectively complete, with solo developer Robson Paiva only planning on adding a hard mode and tuning balance between now and launch. See it in motion in the trailer below.
